_meta.harness: run-evals.mjs --set eval-set-v2.json (the golden-set lineage, extended with an LLM judge — see _meta.harnessDecision)
_meta.harnessDecision: BUILT INTO run-evals.mjs, NOT run-l2-evals.mjs, and NOT a third runner. Reasons, in order: (1) V2 is explicitly a golden-set SUCCESSOR ('anchors require verification before this becomes golden-set.json'), so it belongs in that lineage and inherits cardCheck + the deterministic numeric scorer; (2) the capability it lacked — an LLM judge — is ADDED to that harness by porting the judge from run-l2-evals.mjs, which starts CLOSING the two-harness split rather than widening it to three; (3) run-l2-evals computes ground truth from metrics_daily, which V2 section 3 rules out as circular for exactly the adversarial questions this set exists to ask. See ★TWO-EVAL-HARNESSES-ONE-JUDGE.
_meta.groundTruth: TWO TRUTH SOURCES, AND THEY ARE NOT EQUAL. (1) BEHAVIOUR — 30 questions (assert.type='boundary') are graded on whether the answer names the boundary/gap and bounds its claim. These need NO external value and are the strongest thing in this set. (2) CAPTURED STORE — 48 questions were repointed onto windows the coverage instrument reads COMPLETE at the grain the question needs, and their truthSource is literally 'captured store, coverage COMPLETE for this window'. (3) 20 remain UNGRADED and 2 UNSCORED.
_meta.gradeableTonight: The 21 adversarial + 4 calibration questions, minus D20 and E16 (unscored per V2) = 23. Those are gradeable WITHOUT external ground truth because the correct behaviour is 'name the boundary / name the gap / bound the claim', which is checkable from the answer alone.

_meta.thePattern: OUR FLOOR IS OLDER THAN THE VENDOR'S ON EVERY PLATFORM WHERE WE HAVE BEEN CAPTURING. That is the product thesis — banked-and-growing capture outlives the vendor's rolling window — and three of the four falsified premises inverted it, classifying as a WALL a window we actually hold. A vendor wall bounds BACKFILL, never what is already captured.

_meta.whyStoreTruthIsWeaker: ⛔ STORE TRUTH IS WEAKER THAN A PLATFORM READ AND MUST BE REPLACED BEFORE ANYTHING GOES TO AN OUTSIDE EVALUATOR. It is partially circular: it measures whether Lora can faithfully retrieve and reason over what we captured, NOT whether what we captured matches what the platform actually reported. A systematic capture bug — a wrong dedup, a timezone slip, a metric mapped to the wrong column — would be invisible, because the eval and the system under test would share the same error. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH DOING ANYWAY, and this is the point of deriving the windows rather than skipping correctness: ON A WINDOW THE INSTRUMENT CALLS COMPLETE, THE STORE AND THE PLATFORM SHOULD AGREE. Every base-active day carries its rows, nothing is mid-drain, nothing is past a retention wall. So a later platform read that DISAGREES with one of these 48 is not an eval failure — IT IS A CAPTURE FINDING, and a sharper one than a mismatch on a partial window, where disagreement would be expected and uninformative. The 48 are therefore a standing bet: each one is a place where a future platform read is guaranteed to be diagnostic. REPLACE THEM PLATFORM-BY-PLATFORM AS GROUND TRUTH IS COLLECTED; do not quote their pass rate as an accuracy figure in the meantime.

denominators.note: Any percentage MUST name which of the two truth sources it rests on. A rate over the 30 is a BEHAVIOUR result. A rate over the 48 is a RETRIEVAL result against our own store. They are different claims and neither is 'accuracy' for the 100.

_meta.instrumentCaveat: Windows were derived through a direct pg session with a 600s statement_timeout, reimplementing resolveBreakdownCoverage's own definition over the same two day-sets the RPC returns. THE LIVE INSTRUMENT IS BOUND BY THE 8s PostgREST CEILING and returns UNKNOWN above it — Foam OH meta is a known offender. So a window called COMPLETE here may read UNKNOWN on the live path. That is a difference in the INSTRUMENT, not in the data, and it is why ★BREAKDOWN-COVERAGE-UNKNOWN-CONFLATES-TIMEOUT matters.

questions.message: Forecast next quarter from captured data and the uploaded targets. State your uncertainty.

assert.rubric: A forecast is a claim about a period with no data at all, so the uncertainty statement is the substance of the answer, not a footnote. assert.mustNotAssert: A point forecast presented without uncertainty, or a confidence range asserted as if it were derived from a model when it is not.

(2) Q2 2023 is before Foam OH's Meta capture floor of 2023-06-21 AND at/behind the 37-month aggregate wall (2023-07-01), and creative attribution for 2023-06-21→2023-07-28 is separately recorded as permanently gone. A passing answer names the capability limit and the retention boundary as DIFFERENT things.
assert.mustNotAssert: A specific asset combination tied to revenue for that window, or a claim that the combination data merely needs to be fetched. V2 calls this the single most important question in the set.
